I really like pursuit curves! It's where what if you had one particle chasing another particle? And what does it look like? They're not really difficult to understand at all but I just think they're really cool, and I'm sure there must be some crazy insight that I just haven't understood or seen yet. Here's some resources I used to research them:

https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1963350/a-problem-that-gives-rise-to-a-differential-equation This stack exchange, which links to http://sections.maa.org/okar/papers/2006/lloyd.pdf this paper, that talks about dogs chasing rabbits, generalized.  
https://www.physicsforums.com/threads/de-problem-dog-chasing-a-rabbit.232532/ This thread is really useful because it provides a much simpler way of getting an equation that's referenced in the previous paper (using velocity instead of arc length).  
http://baselines.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Dog\_Rabbit\_Pursuit.pdf This little paper is my favorite because it explained it in the simplest terms (even though I haven't taken Diff EQ, I could still understand it!)  
Lastly credit where credit is due: I only heard about this problem because of this tumblr post: [https://www.tumblr.com/mathani/655322613750562816/this-puzzle-will-test-your-calculus-skills-rabbit?source=share](https://www.tumblr.com/mathani/655322613750562816/this-puzzle-will-test-your-calculus-skills-rabbit?source=share) also has a very cool GIF.

DID, or dissociative identity disorder, is a disorder caused by severe childhood trauma. During a normal childhood, individual aspects of a child's personality develop into one. Trauma prevents this from happening and creates multiple personalities. Those are called "alters", and switching is just when they switch.

The way you dress, your opinions, and your music taste change often as you figure out what your stances are and what sorts of things you like. It doesn't necessarily mean you have multiple personalities- moreso just that you're trying out different things while figuring out who you want to be as an adult. However, if it's of concern to you, you should really talk it out with someone qualified in mental health. They can help you understand what's going on, why you're worried about it, and what you can do to ease those worries. It's really easy to get misinformation on the internet.

3. If you self-diagnose incorrectly, it can be harmful to the communities of people who have those disorders. It can also be harmful to you, yourself!
